title: LRU cache: evict the least recently used
summary: An OrderedDict keeps keys from least to most recently used. get and put move the key to the end; when the cache overflows, popitem(last=False) evicts from the front. O(1) per operation.
code: # Keys run from least to most recently used: a touch moves a key to the end, eviction takes the front.
triggers: a fixed-size cache that evicts whatever was used longest ago
O(1) get and put that also track recency: a hash map plus an ordered list
prompts: A photo app keeps thumbnails for the 200 images viewed most recently. Opening an old image again must protect it from being the next one dropped.
A database client caches query results but has room for a few hundred. When it's full, it discards the result nobody has asked for in the longest time.
invariant: items holds at most capacity keys ordered from least to most recently used, and every get or put moves its key to the end.
mantra: Touch moves to the back; evict from the front.
pitfalls: popitem() takes the newest entry by default; LRU eviction needs popitem(last=False).
Assigning to an existing key keeps its old position, so move it to the end after updating.
Without OrderedDict, use a dict of nodes and a doubly linked list with head and tail sentinels.

anchors.name: LRU Cache
anchors.trick: Exactly this; interviewers may ask for the linked-list version.

anchors.name: LFU Cache
anchors.trick: Group keys by use count, with LRU order inside each count.

mutations.explanation: popitem() takes from the end by default, evicting the key that was just put instead of the least recently used one.
Moving a read key to the front marks it least recent, so the key you just used is evicted next.
